resource: Monster summons per creature: max_summons, summon entries and the count of one entry
allocation_impact: Content validation refuses a creature with more than 16 summons (max_summons) or more than 8 summon entries; the carrier refuses a child past the parent's authored total or per-creature count (admit_native_summon). The channel-wide summon state scales with it per live creature: the native summon owner keeps at most CREATUREAI0-RL-04 creatures times 8 entries replay memos (NATIVE_SUMMON_MEMOS_PER_CHANNEL_MAX, 2,097,152), and the defence summon owner and the creature self-heal ledger at most CREATUREAI0-RL-04 creatures times the 8 defences of CREATUREAI0-RL-07 (CREATURE_DEFENCE_MEMOS_PER_CHANNEL_MAX). Each is an ActorMemoTable keyed by the exact creature and its entry in ordered maps (Codex 4243039220): a creature's first touch drops what its slot's former occupant left, and a full table drops dead creatures' memos before it refuses, so no lookup or insert passes over every memo. These replace the D57 envelope of 64 creatures times 8.
boundary_tests: max=16 summons and 8 entries: an authored summon set within both passes the profile schedule
max+1: max_summons 17, an entry count of 17 or a 9th summon entry is refused (InvalidSummonFacts, TooManyEntries)
channel scale: 100 summoners (more than the old 64-creature envelope) each summon, retire their dead children together and summon again
consumers: apps/game-server/src/content/project/v2/creature.rs v2 creature summons validation (max_summons <= 16, entries <= 8) and ai_think/profile_schedule.rs summon facts
apps/game-server/src/monster_summon.rs NativeSummonOwner and DefenseSummonOwner replay memos
